This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **37** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 150da61aa54c6a287bdc834db3b13399d18e50d9`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `refuseUnknownQueryParams (9 routes)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 150da61aa54c6a287bdc834db3b13399d18e50d9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1408904256333014658b921c67ea6c87fe6bcdd1` — the merge of head `6fe8e7462997a86173eedf17e0625062bdebfd76` into base `150da61aa54c6a287bdc834db3b13399d18e50d9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 1408904256333014658b921c67ea6c87fe6bcdd1 && git checkout 1408904256333014658b921c67ea6c87fe6bcdd1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 150da61aa54c6a287bdc834db3b13399d18e50d9 6fe8e7462997a86173eedf17e0625062bdebfd76 && git checkout -B drift-repro 150da61aa54c6a287bdc834db3b13399d18e50d9 && git merge --no-ff 6fe8e7462997a86173eedf17e0625062bdebfd76

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 150da61aa54c6a287bdc834db3b13399d18e50d9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, named right or wrong against the handlers' ACTUAL read points on both transports.

1. **One decision (ruling B) — right, with one residual named.** `metaItemQueryRefusal(door, query)` in `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts` holds the per-door table (`accepted` and `once`), the recognition sentence (`unknownQueryParamRefusalMessage`, imported), the arity sentence (`repeatedQueryParamMessage`, imported) and the layered-member sentence, in the order recognition, arity, layered-member. `domains/meta.ts` carries no second spelling: its four doors call the decision and read nothing else from the query but `package` (`metaItemPackageBinding`), `mode` (`metaSaveRequestOptions`, whose only query read is `http.query?.mode`), `state`, `preview`, `layers` (`wantsMetaItemLayers`), `locale` (`metaRequestLocale` behind `answerMetaItem`) and `member` (`metaMemberSelector`). `rest-server.ts`'s item GET carries none: its two gate lines and the hand-spelled arity list `['layers', 'state', 'preview', 'package', member]` are gone, and the five constants it re-exports are declared once in the gate module. The residual: `RestServer`'s `PUT` (`:7124`-`:7125`, arity `['force', 'package', 'mode']`) and `serveMetaItemLayered` (`:4026`, arity `['package']`) keep slice 1's own gate lines, so those two arity lists are spelled once more there than in the decision's `once` table. They are not this PR's lines, the claim re-points `RestServer`'s item GET only, the ruling's re-point sentence names the item GET only, and the SETS (the thing that narrows) are one source. Recorded for the seat as a follow-up under the ruling's own rationale (a name added later should reach both transports): a one-line re-point each, or a fifth door that reads `force`, in a later slice. Not a defect at this head.
2. **The item read's closed set on BOTH transports = `layers`, `state`, `preview`, `package`, `locale`, `member` — right.** Dispatcher read points, measured on `handleMetadataRequest`'s two-segment branch at this head: `state` (`:1611`), `preview` (`:1619`), `package` (`packageBinding()`, now called after the decision), `layers` (`:1660`, and rule 3), `locale` (`answerMetaItem` `:650` builds `metaRequestLocale({ headers, query })`, and `readPendingDraft` hands its `query` to the same chain), `member` (`:1604`). No name the handler reads is outside the set (no new false 400), and no name in the set goes unread (no silent drop). `locale` is accepted and deliberately outside the `once` list, as on `RestServer`: `metaRequestLocale`'s typeof guard sends a repeated value to the default, pinned in the new rest file. `member` is accepted on the item read alone and refused by the other three doors, pinned per door.
3. **`PUT` on the dispatcher = `package`, `mode` — right, and derived.** `META_ITEM_SAVE_UNFORCED_PARAMS` is `META_ITEM_SAVE_PARAMS.filter(name !== 'force')`, frozen, not hand-kept. The branch reads `package` through the binding and `mode` through `metaSaveRequestOptions`, and nothing else: the grep of `:1377`-`:1520` for `query` finds exactly those two reads. `force` is read nowhere on this transport (`:1429`-`:1449`: the #11095 ruling, settled, with the 409 remedy saying the door accepts no `force`), so refusing it is the honest answer and dropping it was the defect. `RestServer`'s own `PUT` keeps `META_ITEM_SAVE_PARAMS` with `force`, untouched.
4. **`/layers` = `package`, `/published` = empty — right on both transports.** The dispatcher's `/layers` reads `query?.package` once (`:1109`) and hands `answerMetaLayered` no query; its `/published` branch (`:1125`-`:1260`) reads no query key at all. `RestServer`'s sets are slice 1's, unchanged, and the dispatcher's doors read the same constants.
5. **`RestServer`'s item GET is byte-identical — the claim holds on the diff, not only on the dev's differential.** Rules 1 and 2: the old `refuseUnknownQueryParams` body is now `unknownQueryParamRefusalMessage` verbatim (same object check, same sorted unknown list, same `unknownQueryParamMessage(unknown, sorted allowed)`), and the old `refuseRepeatedQueryParams` loop is reproduced line for line in the decision (same object check, same iteration order over the same five names, `readSingleQueryValue`, the same `repeatedQueryParamMessage(name, count)`, the same in-place `record[name] = read.value`). The handler writes them as `res.status(400).json({ error: { code, message } })`, the nested body both gates wrote. Rule 3: the predicate is the same `wantsMetaItemLayers(query) && member !== undefined` on the post-unwrap query, the sentence is the same template with `META_ITEM_MEMBER_PARAM`, it is thrown at the same position (after `resolveProtocol`, `metaTypeSingular` and the mask posture, before the layered branch) as an `Error` carrying the same `code` and `status`, to the same `handleRouteError`, which writes the same flat body. No header is written by any of the three rules; the `Deprecation` and `Link` headers come after rule 3, unchanged. Order relative to the anonymous deny (the auth middleware at `:2374`, before every handler), the per-caller read gate (inside the branches after rule 3) and the mask posture (between rules 2 and 3) is unchanged, because the diff's two hunks in this handler touch only the top gate lines and the rule-3 throw, and the lines between are not in the diff. `memberSelector` is read after the unwrap, as before. The new rest file pins nested for rules 1 and 2 and flat for rule 3, with the protocol never called; the member-selector and closed-sets files are not in the diff. The 480-record differential is consistent with all of this; it was not re-run and is not needed.
6. **The dispatcher item read with `?member=` — right; a named member is never answered with the canonical item.** The selector reaches all three `getMetaItem` calls: the draft read (`readPendingDraft`, `...item.memberSelector`), the `object` branch (`:1739`) and the generic branch (`:1795`). With a member named: `protocolFirst` is true (`:1725`), the `object` branch's bare `catch` rethrows (`:1755`), the registry read is guarded by `!memberNamed` (`:1761`), a protocol without `getMetaItem` falls to the branch's own 404; the generic branch's `catch` rethrows (`:1829`) and `MetadataService` is never resolved (`:1839`), so an absent member is the 404 and a protocol refusal reaches the outer `catch`, whose `errorFromThrown(e, 404)` keeps a thrown `status` and a registered `code` (`resolveThrownHttpError`: `declaredStatus` wins over the fallback), pinned against a real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` (a `view` and an `object` answer the protocol's located 400; a blank selector is refused). `?layers=` beside a member is rule 3, before any read. With NO member named: `...{}` spreads nothing into any request, `memberNamed` is false so every guard reverts to its old expression, both catches swallow as before, and `MetadataService` is resolved as before (control pinned). The one behaviour a member-less request gains beside the two intended refusals is the arity rule's in-place unwrap: a name supplied once as a one-element array (`{ state: ['draft'] }`) now reads as the string, where it read as absent. That is `RestServer`'s own behaviour since #6877, the acceptance notes declare the mutation, and the published Hono host never builds an array. Right.
7. **Refusal ordering vs authorization — right, with one placement difference declared.** On the dispatcher the anonymous deny (`:937`) and the type-level read and write refusals (`:947`-`:970`) precede every branch, so all four decisions answer after them: no caller gets a 400 where it got the 401 or the type-level 403. `PUT`'s decision sits after the capability 403 and the walled-catalog 403 (`:1340`, `:1365`) and before `metaSaveRequestOptions`, the protocol resolve and the 501, with the capability gate pinned to answer first; `RestServer`'s sits after its 501. `/layers`' decision is the branch's first statement, before the protocol, the mask and the 501; `RestServer` refuses recognition first and arity after its 501. `/published` is first statement on both. The item read answers rules 1 and 2 after the 405 verb check and before the mask posture, and rule 3 after it, as `RestServer` does. The one caller who can reach a decision unauthenticated is the public-audience exemption on a `book` or `doc` item read, on both transports alike; the refusal body is static (the unknown name and the fixed set), so it is no existence or capability oracle, and nothing a prior gate withholds is reachable through it. What changes between transports is only the 400-versus-501 order for a caller who already passed the capability gate on `PUT`, or sends a repeated `package` to a host with no layered read on `/layers`. Judged in ③.
8. **The published surface — right as graded; one consistency note.** `packages/rest/package.json` publishes the single `.` entry (`dist/index.*`, no `private`), and `src/index.ts` gains exactly two value names, `metaItemQueryRefusal` and `metaMemberSelector`, in the gate module's existing value block. Nothing left the entry (the index diff is +9 / -0). None of the five `META_ITEM_*` constants joined it (zero hits in `index.ts`); they are module exports re-exported from `rest-server.ts` so slice 1's two test files import them unchanged. `unknownQueryParamRefusalMessage` is a module export of `query-allowlist.ts` that the entry does not re-export (the entry takes nothing from that module). The two types `MetaItemQueryDoor` and `MetaItemQueryRefusal` are module exports left out of the entry's `export type` block; under the shared tsup `dts` bundling they are emitted as local declarations beside the two functions, so a consumer gets the full structural type by inference and may name it only by deriving it, which is what `domains/meta.ts` does (`NonNullable` of the function's `ReturnType`). Usable, and within the ruling's one-to-two exports. The note: the sibling decisions' types (`MetaTypeReadRefusal`, `MetaTypeWriteRefusal`, `MetaItemReadRefusal`) ARE on that `export type` block, so this pair is the odd one out; adding the two names later is a `type-surface-only` widening. The seat's call, not a finding.
9. **`query-allowlist.ts` — right.** `refuseUnknownQueryParams` now calls the extracted pure function and writes the same 400, the same nested envelope and the same message; the extraction moved the old body verbatim, and `unknownQueryParamMessage`, which every route's sentence comes from, is not touched. Every existing route keeps its exact answer.
10. **The objectui force-save path at the console pin — a changed failure, and the wider class is declared.** The dispatcher never read `force` (item 3), so the post-409 retry Studio sends on a dispatcher-only host already failed with the protocol's 409; it now fails with the located 400 naming `force` before any save. No flow that worked goes red. The class the changeset declares beyond Studio: a caller who passes `force: true` pre-emptively on a non-destructive save through a dispatcher-only host went 200 on `main` (the name dropped, the save fine) and answers 400 now. That is exactly the narrowing the card exists to make loud, it is BREAKING and the changeset's `PUT` line carries its remedy (drop `?force=`). The census (the SDK sends `force` only on `force: true`; no in-repo production caller does; record `6138381862` item 8 measured Studio at the same pin) is consistent with the diff.
11. **The caller census — holds on what this tree can show.** `@objectstack/client`'s `metaSaveQuery` emits `force`, `package`, `mode`; `getItem` sends `package`; `getPublished` nothing; no `/layers` caller; the conformance and hono suites that boot `createHonoApp` with the real dispatcher are in the head's `Test Core` shards, which are green.
12. **The parity pins — right.** `meta-list-projection-parity`'s `ITEM_PROBES` gains `?member=zh-CN` and `?layers=true&member=zh-CN`, its protocol double refuses a member on every non-bundle type as the protocol's first step does, and the reference-moves pin shows `?member=` reaching the protocol on `RestServer`. The new runtime file compares each dispatcher refusal's code and message with `RestServer`'s for the same request on the item read, `/layers` and `/published`, and pins `PUT`'s own two-name sentence.

### ② Semver level

**Right.** Judged against AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, the two changeset gates' sources, and PR #23133's records.

- `'@objectstack/rest': minor` — two new value exports widen the published entry; `Clause-②: yes` takes at least `minor`. Right.
- `'@objectstack/runtime': minor` — four dispatcher accept sets narrow, which is BREAKING, shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention the no-major gate's header states; the same grade slice 1 landed with and the records `6138381862` and `6139157658` ruled. The only malformed arm is `no (widening)`, which this head does not use. Right.

Each checked against the diff: `packages/spec` is untouched, no `*.object.ts` moves, the index diff removes nothing, the only `adr-0087` string in the diff is the marker. ### ③ Boundary flags

The report `6142050405` has no `open_questions`, which is right: the one question slice 1 raised (`6137337775`, A / B / C) is answered by ruling B `6138588561`, and this head is that answer. Every dev flag and every finding, answered or escalated:
